topics.name: Topic 1 The changing landscapes of the UK
points: 1.1 There are geological variations within the UK
1.2 A number of physical and human processes work together to create distinct UK landscapes

topics.name: Topic 1A Coastal landscapes and processes (option)
points: 1.3 A variety of physical processes interact to shape coastal landscapes
1.4 Coastal erosion and deposition create distinctive landforms within the coastal landscape
1.5 Human activities can lead to changes in coastal landscapes which affect people and the environment
1.6 Distinctive coastal landscapes are the outcome of the interaction between physical and human processes

topics.name: Topic 1B River landscapes and processes (option)
points: 1.7 A variety of physical processes interact to shape river landscapes
1.8 Erosion and deposition interacting with geology create distinctive landforms in river landscapes
1.9 Human activities can lead to changes in river landscapes which affect people and the environment
1.10 Distinctive river landscapes are the outcome of the interaction between physical and human processes

topics.name: Topic 1C Glaciated upland landscapes and processes (option)
points: 1.11 A variety of physical processes interact to shape glaciated upland landscapes
1.12 Glacial erosion and deposition create distinctive landforms within glaciated upland landscapes
1.13 Human activities can lead to changes in glaciated upland landscapes
1.14 Distinctive glaciated upland landscapes are the outcome of the interaction between physical and human processes

topics.name: Topic 2 Weather hazards and climate change
points: 2.1 The atmosphere operates as a global system transferring heat and energy
2.2 The global climate was different in the past and continues to change due to natural causes
2.3 Global climate is now changing as a result of human activity
2.4 The UK has a distinct climate which has changed over time
2.5 Tropical cyclones are extreme weather events that develop under specific conditions and in certain locations
2.6 Impacts of and responses to tropical cyclones depending on a country's level of development
2.7 The causes of drought are complex with some locations more vulnerable than others
2.8 The impacts of, and responses to, drought vary depending on a country's level of development

topics.name: Topic 3 Ecosystems, biodiversity and management
points: 3.1 Large-scale ecosystems are found in different parts of the world and are important
3.2 The biosphere is a vital system
3.3 The UK has its own variety of distinctive ecosystems that it relies on
3.4 Tropical rainforests show a range of distinguishing features
3.5 Tropical rainforest ecosystems provide a range of goods and services, some of which are under threat
3.6 Deciduous woodlands show a range of distinguishing features
3.7 Deciduous woodland ecosystems provide a range of goods and services, some of which are under threat

topics.name: Topic 4 Changing cities
points: 4.1 Urbanisation is a global process
4.2 The degree of urbanisation varies across the UK
4.3 UK city case study: the context of the chosen UK city influences its functions and structure
4.4 UK city case study: the city is being changed by movements of people, employment and services
4.5 UK city case study: globalisation and economic change create challenges that require long-term solutions
4.6 Developing/emerging country city case study: context influences its functions and structure
4.7 Developing/emerging country city case study: character influenced by its fast rate of growth
4.8 Developing/emerging country city case study: rapid growth results in challenges that need to be managed

topics.name: Topic 5 Global development
points: 5.1 Definitions of development vary as do attempts to measure it
5.2 The level of development varies globally
5.3 Uneven global development has had a range of consequences
5.4 A range of strategies has been used to try to address uneven development
5.5 Country case study: level of development influenced by its location and context in the world
5.6 Country case study: interactions of economic, social and demographic processes influence development
5.7 Country case study: changing geopolitics and technology impact on the chosen country
5.8 Country case study: positive and negative impacts of rapid development for people and environment

topics.name: Topic 6 Resource management
points: 6.1 A natural resource is any feature or part of the environment that can be used to meet human needs
6.2 Patterns of distribution and consumption of natural resources vary on a global and a national scale

topics.name: Topic 6A Energy resource management (option)
points: 6.3 Renewable and non-renewable energy resources can be developed
6.4 Countries use energy resources in different proportions: the energy mix
6.5 Increasing demand for energy is being met by renewable and non-renewable resources
6.6 Meeting the demands for energy resources can involve interventions by different interest groups
6.7 Management and sustainable use of energy resources at a range of spatial scales from local to international

topics.name: Topic 6B Water resource management (option)
points: 6.8 The supply of fresh water varies globally
6.9 Differences between water consumption patterns of developing and developed countries
6.10 Countries at different levels of development have water supply problems
6.11 Meeting the demands for water can involve technology and interventions by different interest groups
6.12 Management and sustainable use of water resources at a range of spatial scales from local to international

papers.name: Paper 3 Geographical Investigations: Fieldwork and UK Challenges

topics.name: Topic 7A Investigating physical environments: rivers (fieldwork option)
points: Task: investigation of change in a river channel; formulating enquiry questions
Fieldwork methods: quantitative measurement of river discharge and qualitative recording of river landforms
Implications of river processes for people in the catchment
Secondary data: flood risk map (e.g. Environment Agency) and one other source
Presenting, analysing, concluding and evaluating the river enquiry

topics.name: Topic 7A Investigating physical environments: coasts (fieldwork option)
points: Task: investigation of coastal processes through landscape evidence; formulating enquiry questions
Fieldwork methods: quantitative measurement of beach morphology and sediment characteristics; qualitative recording of coastal landforms
Implications of coastal processes for people living in the coastal environment
Secondary data: geology map (e.g. BGS Geology of Britain viewer) and one other source
Presenting, analysing, concluding and evaluating the coastal enquiry

topics.name: Topic 7B Investigating human environments: central/inner urban area (fieldwork option)
points: Task: investigating change in central/inner urban area(s); formulating enquiry questions
Fieldwork methods: qualitative recording of urban environmental quality and quantitative measurement of land use function
Interactions between physical landscape features, the area, and residents and visitors
Secondary data: census data (e.g. ONS) and one other source
Presenting, analysing, concluding and evaluating the urban enquiry

topics.name: Topic 7B Investigating human environments: rural settlements (fieldwork option)
points: Task: investigating change in rural settlements; formulating enquiry questions
Fieldwork methods: qualitative recording of people's views on rural environmental quality and quantitative measurement of flows of people
Interactions between physical landscape features, the settlement, and residents and visitors
Secondary data: ONS neighbourhood statistics and one other source
Presenting, analysing, concluding and evaluating the rural enquiry

topics.name: Topic 8 Geographical investigations: UK challenges
points: 8.1 The UK's resource consumption and environmental sustainability challenge
8.2 The UK settlement, population and economic challenges
8.3 The UK's landscape challenges
8.4 The UK's climate change challenges
